title: Understanding the Component Lifecycle knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Understanding the Component Lifecycle”?
options: Understanding the Component Lifecycle means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Understanding the Component Lifecycle removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Understanding the Component Lifecycle should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Understanding the Component Lifecycle helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Understanding the Component Lifecycle helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Understanding the Component Lifecycle is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Component creation and initialization” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Component creation and initialization” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Component creation and initialization” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Component creation and initialization” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Component creation and initialization” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Component creation and initialization” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Component creation and initialization” under Understanding the Component Lifecycle. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Understanding the Component Lifecycle”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
